problem_summary.summary: Check whether equal values occur at two distinct indices no more than k positions apart.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: integer array nums and nonnegative integer k. Return true if any pair of equal values has index distance at most k.

brute_force.explanation: For each index, inspect later indices only as far as k positions away and compare values.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every possible pair satisfying the distance bound is visited by the nested loops. The method returns true exactly when one such pair has equal values.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n * min(n, k)) worst case, where n is the array length.

optimized.explanation: Scan from left to right and store the latest index for each value. If the current index minus the stored index is at most k, a nearby duplicate exists; otherwise update the latest index.
optimized.correctness_idea: For any value, its latest prior occurrence gives the smallest possible distance to the current index. If even that distance exceeds k, no earlier occurrence can qualify; storing the latest position preserves the best check for future elements.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n) expected, with one scan and expected constant-time map operations.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary in the worst case for the latest index of each distinct value.

steps.condition: A previous index exists and distance 2 <= k 2.
steps.action: Return true immediately; the map remains unchanged.

edge_cases.handling: Distinct indices cannot have distance zero, so no pair qualifies.

edge_cases.case: Same value repeats just beyond k
edge_cases.handling: The previous occurrence fails the distance check and the map is updated to the newer index.
The full scan completes and returns false.
